The active-artifact totals are calculated solely from the manifest's recorded `byte_length` values, without reading any of the output paths or checking their recorded hashes. Consequently, deleting or corrupting an artifact such as `semantic-registry.json` leaves the manifest unchanged and `--check` still prints `KG-N0 scaling baseline: PASS`, even though the checked-in active snapshot has drifted. Validate every manifest output against its actual byte length and SHA-256 before accepting the baseline.

When `--output` is relative or resolves beneath `--repo`, these lines create and write that path without enforcing the runner's stated no-repository-write posture. A caller can therefore commit a generated benchmark packet or, more seriously, overwrite one of the immutable historical artifacts after all zero-write profiling checks have completed. Resolve the destination first and reject repository descendants, requiring an external output such as the documented `/tmp` path.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Exercise tampering against the P1 manifest too**

Every corruption case passed to this helper is applied only to `P3_MANIFEST`; the P1 manifest is always a pristine symlink. Thus the suite still passes if the runtime stops authenticating appended bytes or stale identity in the P1 manifest, despite presenting this as a P1/P3 compatibility baseline and relying on a separate P1 authentication path. Parameterize which manifest is transformed and run the relevant negative cases for P1 as well.
